topic: The Path from Violence to Self-Acceptance

facts.label: Story
facts.value: The Path from Violence to Self-Acceptance

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Guest Post from Pete Bates, The Pete Bates Project I wasn’t swinging because I was physically threatened. I was swinging because I was intellectually threatened. That’s something it took me a very long time to understand about myself. When I was a young man, I didn’t know how to argue without becoming aggressive. I didn’t know how to properly articulate what I was thinking, explain what I was feeling, or defend a position when somebody challenged me. I could feel something strongly without having the language to explain why. And when somebody could articulate themselves better than I could, I often experienced that as humiliation. I wasn’t necessarily frightened of the person standing in front of me. I was frightened of being exposed. Exposed as somebody who couldn’t find the words. Somebody who couldn’t construct an argument. Somebody who couldn’t explain himself without becoming frustrated, defensive or angry. And instead of recognising that limitation, I’d turn the situation into something I understood. A physical confrontation. I couldn’t win the argument with my words, so I’d try to end it with my fists. For a long time, I confused that with strength. It wasn’t strength. It was a failure in the way I had learnt to respond to being challenged. And I want to make something absolutely clear. That doesn’t excuse a single act of violence.

en.headline: The Path from Violence to Self-Acceptance

topic: Crunch Fitness Seeks to Borrow $800 Million in ABS Bond Sale

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Crunch Fitness Seeks to Borrow $800 Million in ABS Bond Sale

facts.label: Article
facts.value: The offering may kick off as soon as next week after early talks with some investors, according to people with knowledge of the matter (Bloomberg) — Crunch Fitness is looking to raise about $800 million from a bond sale backed by the company’s franchise revenue, adding to a string of companies tapping the whole-business securitization market in recent weeks. The offering may kick off as soon as next week after early talks with some investors, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The financing would include $650 million of bonds with an average life of about five years marketed to institutional investors, a $100 million privately placed note that can be drawn at a later date, and a $50 million variable funding facility, the people said. Guggenheim Securities is leading the deal, they added, asking not to be identified because they’re not authorized to speak publicly. Early price discussions on the five-year bonds are for spreads of 2.3 to 2.5 percentage points over benchmark rates, the people said. The plans and details haven’t been finalized and may still change, they added. A spokesperson for Guggenheim declined to comment. A representative for Crunch didn’t respond to a request for comment. Planet Fitness Inc.’s securitized debt provides one comparison for Crunch’s proposed pricing.

en.headline: Crunch Fitness Seeks to Borrow $800 Million in ABS Bond Sale

topic: HFA Unveils Three-Year Strategic Vision to Strengthen Member Value and Advance the Health and Fitness Industry

facts.label: Story
facts.value: HFA Unveils Three-Year Strategic Vision to Strengthen Member Value and Advance the Health and Fitness Industry

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Greta Wagner named permanent president and CEO after six months of strategic planning, organizational alignment, and renewed focus on the association’s future. WASHINGTON, DC, November 12, 2026 — The The Health & Fitness Association (HFA) today announced a new strategic plan and vision designed to strengthen the association, deliver greater value to its members, and expand its influence as the leading voice of the global health and fitness industry. The announcement marks an important milestone after six months of focused work to evaluate the association’s priorities, engage industry leaders, align its leadership team, and establish a clear roadmap for the future. HFA also announced that Greta Wagner has accepted the permanent role of president and CEO, providing continuity of leadership as the association moves decisively from strategy development to execution. The announcement was made on stage at Beyond Activ Americas in Dallas on November 12, before an audience of 950 industry executives. Over the past six months, HFA has undertaken a comprehensive review of how the association serves its members, supports their businesses, and represents the broader industry.

en.headline: HFA Unveils Three-Year Strategic Vision to Strengthen Member Value and Advance the Health and Fitness Industry

topic: With $3.5M in funding, Betterness wants to turn Miami neighborhoods into wellness networks

facts.label: Story
facts.value: With $3.5M in funding, Betterness wants to turn Miami neighborhoods into wellness networks

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Facebook Tweet Pin LinkedIn Email Seven months ago, Miami-based Betterness was building an AI-powered health coach that could help people manage their wellness routines. Now, the startup wants to take that concept beyond the smartphone and into the neighborhoods where people actually live, work and exercise. Betterness has secured an additional $1 million in seed financing, bringing its total seed round to $3.5 million. The funding comes as the company prepares to launch its first neighborhood wellness network at Miami Worldcenter on November 15, bringing together more than 30 local businesses through a new initiative called Worldcenter Perks. The extension was led by a private investment group with pharmaceutical expertise, alongside investors with backgrounds in AI, venture capital, healthcare, and blockchain. When Refresh Miami last covered Betterness in April , the company had raised $2.5 million and was positioning itself as an AI-powered platform connecting consumers, healthcare providers, gyms and wellness brands. At the center was Bett-i, an AI life coach designed to draw on data from wearables, lab results and other sources to help users make better health decisions. Since then, Betterness has moved its business customers from beta testing into daily operations.

en.headline: With $3.5M in funding, Betterness wants to turn Miami neighborhoods into wellness networks

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Das Hamburger Unternehmen Fitvertise bündelt Werbung in mehr als 2.200 Studios. Betreiber beteiligen sich ohne Kosten an den Werbeerlösen, während Marken analoge und digitale Formate zentral buchen können. In den Fitnessstudios kommt von diesem Geld bislang kaum etwas an. Marken können die Formate bundesweit über einen Ansprechpartner buchen. Zum Netzwerk gehören unter anderem die LifeFit Group, EASYFITNESS und zahlreiche inhabergeführte Einzelstudios. Weitere Studios können sich dem Netzwerk unabhängig von ihrer Größe und Kettenzugehörigkeit anschließen. Dazu erklärt Prof. Dr. Karsten Happel, Mitgründer und Geschäftsführer von Fitvertise: „Fitness hat mehr verdient, in der Beachtung wie beim Geld. Deshalb professionalisieren wir die Vermarktung der Studios.“ Die Branche bekommt die Aufmerksamkeit, die ihr zusteht, und die Betreiber bekommen Einnahmen. Ein einzelnes Studio ist für überregionale Werbekunden zu klein für einen Mediaplan.
